bevel-cube-all-round.vertexCount: Where three rounded edges meet, 67.js fills the corner with a triangular patch and Blender uses a quad grid with one centre triangle per corner.
bevel-cube-all-round.faceCount: The triangular corner patch of 67.js has more faces than the quad grid of Blender.
bevel-cube-all-round.faceSizes: The corner patch of 67.js is all triangles. The strips are quads in both.
bevel-cube-all-round.area: The two corner fills are different surfaces. The area differs by 0.3%.
bevel-cube-all-round.positions: The strips match. The inner corner points differ, because the two corner fills are different surfaces.

bevel-cube-one-edge-profile.positions: Both place points on the same superellipse. 67.js steps by equal angle, and Blender spaces them differently when the profile is not 0.5.

bevel-cube-clamped.volume: 67.js clamps at 49% of an edge, because at 50% faces collapse to zero area. Blender clamps at 50% and keeps coincident vertices.
bevel-cube-clamped.area: The 49% clamp of 67.js leaves a slightly larger solid than the 50% clamp of Blender.
bevel-cube-clamped.positions: The 49% clamp of 67.js moves each point 0.014 from where the 50% clamp of Blender puts it.

mirror-touching-plane.faceCount: 67.js removes the wall left on the mirror plane, so the result is one solid. Blender merges the vertices and keeps one inner face.
mirror-touching-plane.faceSizes: 67.js has one quad fewer, because it removes the inner wall on the mirror plane.
mirror-touching-plane.area: Blender counts the inner wall on the mirror plane in the area, and 67.js has no such wall.

array-relative-merged.faceCount: 67.js removes the walls between merged copies, so the result is one solid. Blender merges the vertices and keeps the walls.
array-relative-merged.faceSizes: 67.js has three quads fewer, because it removes the walls between merged copies.
array-relative-merged.volume: The walls that Blender keeps have no single winding, so its signed volume of 5.5 is not the volume of the solid. The 67.js value of 4 is the volume of the solid.
array-relative-merged.area: Blender counts the walls between copies in the area, and 67.js has no such walls.

boolean-through-hole.edgeCount: 67.js has no face with a hole, so it splits a holed face into triangles and quads. Blender keeps one polygon with a seam.
boolean-through-hole.faceCount: A holed face becomes many faces in 67.js and one polygon in Blender. Volume, area and vertices match.
boolean-through-hole.faceSizes: A holed face becomes triangles and quads in 67.js and a 12-sided polygon in Blender.
